subject: Commercial counter-proposal: short decision window for competitive offer
messages:
From: Ellie Barnes <ebarnes@northfield.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northfield.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Northfield: urgent — commercial proposal from HelioStack

Hi Stephanie,

Wanted to flag that we received a hard offer from HelioStack this morning — they
are proposing a 20% effective rate reduction for Year 1 via blended discounts and
6 weeks of migration credits to offset implementation costs. Procurement wants a
formal response from Redwood; they shared their term sheet (attached).

Our renewal window closes on 2026-05-18 and leadership is asking whether Redwood
can provide a competitive onramp within the same timeframe. Key things they care
about: effective unit economics for the first 6 months, any dedicated onboarding
support (hands-on), and guaranteed latency SLOs for our real-time features.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has the flexibility to match or otherwise
structure a near-term commercial concession? We need a clear proposal within the
week if possible.

Thanks —
Ellie Barnes
Director, Platform Engineering
Northfield Logistics

Attachments: heliostack_term_sheet.pdf (term sheet, 6 pages)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Barnes <ebarnes@northfield.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Northfield: urgent — commercial proposal from HelioStack

Hi Ellie,

Thanks for sending this over — appreciate the context and the timeline. I
looped in Rishi (pricing/finance), Monica (CS lead) and Jordan (solutions) so we
can put a crisp counter on your desk quickly. A few quick clarifying questions that
will materially affect structure:

- Current monthly token consumption (avg and 95th pct spikes)?
- Peak qps / concurrent requests for the real-time routing use case?
- Are you looking for an effective blended % across all usage, or specific
  discounts for embeddings vs. generation traffic?
- Any mandatory contract clauses in HelioStack's sheet we should be aware of
  (e.g., data locality, audit windows, termination penalties)?

If you can reply with the numbers, we will run three scenarios and return a
single-page tradeoff matrix showing economics + operational commitments by EOD.

High-level: we generally prefer to protect unit economics with targeted onramp
credits (to offset migration costs) rather than broad upfront discounts, but we
can tailor the approach given your renewal timeline.

I can hop on a 20-minute call today at 1pm PT if that helps expedite.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0136

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Northfield — competitive term sheet (numbers needed)

Folks — forwarding Ellie’s note and the HelioStack sheet. Renewal decision window
is tight (need something by 5/12 ideally). I ran a quick sensitivity and here are
three pragmatic routes we can propose; call out margin and operational impacts: 

Scenario A — 'Parity + Onramp' (conservative margin impact)
- 6-week migration credit applied against invoices (covers egress + setup)
- 15% volume discount for first 12 months (blended across generation + embed)
- Requires no SLA exceptions; minimal legal changes
- Estimated FY1 margin hit: ~12% of expected ARR

Scenario B — 'Dedicated Commitment' (higher near-term commitment)
- 10% standing discount + $50k onboarding credit (one-time)
- Option to add dedicated onboarding engineers (2 weeks) for faster go-live
- Requires 12-month committed minimum and SLA addendum; higher revenue
  predictability
- Estimated FY1 margin hit: ~9% (but more favorable net present value)

Scenario C — 'Short Pilot + Escalator' (low initial hit, risk-managed)
- 8-week pilot credits (offset implementation + egress) then tiered discount
  escalator tied to volume: 5% -> 12% over 3 quarters
- Includes weekly runbook and a single dedicated CS checkpoint during pilot
- Margin hit starts small but climbs if volumes ramp as projected

Attachments: scenario_pnl.xlsx (high-level P&L per scenario)

Operational notes: any option that includes migration credits requires us to
coordinate bandwidth from infra/eng for onboarding. If we commit to 6+ weeks of
credit we should lock a PO or MSA amendment to make the financials recoverable.

Recommendation: I prefer Scenario A as the fastest path to parity and lower
legal friction unless Ellie pushes hard for dedicated engineers — then Scenario B
can be attractive. Open to tweaks.

-Steph

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Barnes <ebarnes@northfield.com>, procurement@northfield.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Northfield: urgent — commercial proposal from HelioStack

Ellie / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the HelioStack sheet and the clarity on timing. After internal
alignment we can put the following near-term commercial on the table if you can
confirm acceptance by 2026-05-12:

Redwood short-window counter (final):
- 8-week migration credit (applied against invoices to offset migration/egress)
- 12% blended volume discount for the first 12 months (generation + embedding)
- Dedicated onboarding support: up to 2 onsite/remote engineer-weeks during the
  onboarding window + weekly checkpoint calls for month 1
- Standard Redwood SLA (we will include a 30-day review clause; no SLA carveouts
  required)

This structure balances a sharp near-term concession (8-week credit) with a
sustained but moderate discount. To proceed we would need a short amendment to
our MSA and a purchase order/intent note specifying the expected start date and
average monthly consumption (so credits can be scheduled). I attached a one-page
term summary for your review.

If you accept, legal can prepare the amendment and Rishi will mirror the credit
and billing schedule in the contract. If you need a slightly larger up-front
credit (6+ weeks) we could explore a higher discount but would need a 12-month
committed minimum.

Can you confirm whether this address will work for leadership and procurement?
We can take the docs to DocuSign same day if needed.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0136
